news.headline: JSW Steel records steel production of 24.65 lakh tonnes in August 2026
news.summary: JSW Steel said that its consolidated crude steel production for the month of August 2026 at 24.65 lakh tonnes, which is higher by 3% as compared with the figure of 23.82 lakh tonnes posted in August 2025.
news.takeaway: JSW Steel said that its consolidated crude steel production for the month of August 2026 at 24.65 lakh; treat it as supply-discipline evidence; India impact travels through sustained Brent direction, not the meeting headline alone.
news.whyItMatters: India imports most of its crude, so the same story can pressure inflation expectations while helping upstream energy.
news.indiaImpact: OMCs, aviation and tyres stay under pressure only if the OPEC+ signal keeps Brent bid; upstream energy is the offset.
news.watchFor: Watch Brent around the Asia handoff; OMC risk stays live only if supply headlines keep prices firm.

news.headline: FII money trail: Where did overseas investors put money in second half of August after $3 billion inflow?
news.summary: Foreign portfolio investors poured over $3.2 billion into Indian equities in August, marking their strongest monthly inflow since September 2024. Consumer Services led buying, followed by Financial Services and Healthcare, while Telecom and Power continued facing significant FPI outflows.
news.takeaway: Foreign portfolio investors poured over $3.2 billion into Indian equities in August, marking their strongest monthly inflow since; institutional flow is the domestic risk check; price still has to confirm it after the first hour.
news.whyItMatters: FII/DII direction can explain whether global cues are being absorbed or rejected by local cash-market demand.
news.indiaImpact: Nifty and Bank Nifty need market participation aligned with FII/DII flow before the morning bias deserves follow-through weight.
news.watchFor: Watch FII/DII provisional flow, Nifty session average and Bank Nifty market participation through 9:45 AM.

news.headline: Tata Motors launches tender offer for Iveco Group; deal values company at €3.82 billion
news.summary: Tata Motors has launched a €14.1-per-share cash tender offer for Iveco Group, valuing the Italian commercial vehicle maker at €3.82 billion. Backed by Iveco’s largest shareholder Exor, the deal targets full acquisition and delisting, amid strong Tata Motors commercial vehicle sales.
news.takeaway: Tata Motors has launched a €14.1-per-share cash tender offer for Iveco Group, valuing the Italian commercial vehicle maker; auto news separates domestic demand from export and input-cost exposure.
news.whyItMatters: Autos can react to volumes, rates, fuel, tariffs or currency; the transmission channel decides the trade.
news.indiaImpact: Nifty Auto and ancillaries need a separate read; tariff or demand news can hit exporters differently from domestic OEMs.
news.watchFor: Watch Nifty Auto market participation, auto-finance names and USD/INR; avoid treating one global EV story as an index cue.
